changes.title: Git workflow: PRs + auto-merge, Check with smoke test, published-files test, size guard
changes.summary:
New standard for working in this repo, for both of us and for Claude sessions. Needs your OK, @vlandham. It changes how we both push.

**Rules** (new "Git workflow" section in CLAUDE.md)
- One short branch per feature, cut from fresh `main`; merge within a day or two
- Unfinished work merges hidden behind a switch (`ready: false`, no `experience`, a dev `?flag`) instead of living on a long branch
- Pull `main` at the start of each session
- Everything reaches `main` through a PR; never push to `main` directly
- **Feature PRs auto-merge** when the Check is green (`gh pr merge --auto --squash --delete-branch`)
- **Shared PRs wait for the other person**: `src/city/`, `App.tsx`, `relay/`, `.github/`, CLAUDE.md, dependencies, `scripts/city/`

**Check workflow** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) on every PR into `main`:
- **Size guard:** no added/changed file over 2 MB unless listed in `.github/large-files.txt` (the four big files already in the repo are listed)
- **Tests**, incl. new `src/content/published.test.ts`: every file the content points at (art, posters, cabinet fronts, game sounds) is in git, so nothing that only lives on one laptop 404s online. The art list is shared with `art:publish` via `scripts/neededArt.mjs`
- **Build**
- **Smoke test** (`npm run smoke`, Playwright): the built site boots with `?solo`, RECENT to the Duck Arcade, opens and closes every playable cabinet; fails on any page error, console error or 404. A missing file was checked to fail it.

After merge: protect `main` (require PRs + a green Check), so auto-merge has something to wait on.

changes.title: Previews: when a PR closes, its preview becomes a "this preview has closed" page
changes.summary:
When a PR closes (merged or not), its preview stops being a live copy of the site.

- **`.github/workflows/preview-cleanup.yml`**, on `pull_request: closed`:
  - re-uploads `pr-<N>` with `preview/closed/index.html`, a short "This preview has closed" page linking to the live site, with no game, relay or idea box;
  - marks the PR's `preview` deployments inactive, so GitHub stops showing an active deployment.
- **Why:** old previews stayed online forever, joining the real relay with old code and able to file real ideas. Cloudflare has no command to delete a preview alias; uploading over one replaces it. It also keeps at most 1,000 aliases per Worker.
- It shares the `preview-<N>` concurrency group with the Preview workflow without cancelling it, so a last upload finishes before the preview is closed.

changes.title: Story log: photos inside scenes, cabinets, dialogs and seasons; tags on every change
changes.summary:
Two additions to the story log.

**1. Photos from inside things, on any build.** `?open=` and `?time=` only exist since #71, so older changes were photographed from the street. Now:
- An `open` place can say where to stand: `open:scene:rush-hour @ 47.5636, -122.3865`. On a build without `?open=` links, the camera stands there with `?at=` and presses {A} until the scene, dialog, ride or mini game is on screen, taking the first choice each time ("Let's see it", "Ride it", "Yes!").
- On a build without the game clock, a place's `time=` is faked in the browser with Playwright's clock. That means the garden can be shown in April on the commit that planted it.
- On builds from before `?at=arcade` worked, the camera starts from the arcade door's coordinates. Those builds used to drop the rabbit nowhere.
- `scripts/story/curated.json` picks places for 22 early changes: inside the Duck Arcade and its cabinets, Rush Hour, Seven+ Stories, the chicken and Cone Catch, the snack crow, Ham, chicken boxing, the Giant Whirl, Sundrop, the garden in November and in April, and the corrected title screen. Curated places win over the guess. `--curated` (always on in the workflow, up to `limit` a run) retakes their photos.
- Each shot records `via: link | way`. Repeated page errors are collapsed into one line with a count.

Tested on real old builds: #65 (garden in November and April), #61 (riding the Whirl), 18e4ad0 (chicken dialog plus Cone Catch), 238fcad (inside the arcade on Nov 4), 2376644 (Rush Hour), 84646d6 (crow), #58 (boxing), #27 (arcade floor). Every "after" photo got in. The "before" photos say `nothing opened` where the thing didn't exist yet.

**2. Tags.** Every change is tagged from what it touched: `wish`, `map`, `character`, `scene`, `arcade`, `art`, `sound`, `words`, `ui`, `multiplayer`, `idea-box`, `code`, `agent`, `story-log`, `infra` and `docs`.
- `code` means the engine and wiring. `agent` means how agents build the island: `scripts/ai`, `CLAUDE.md` rewrites, the guards, and titles about Claude.
- Tags are worked out again for every change on every run, so the old log gets them too.
- A PR's new `Tags:` line, in the template, adds or removes tags (`sound, festival, -code`), and so does `curated.json`.
- The /story/ page has a tag row that filters the log, and tags are shown on each change.

Mike: heads-up. The PR template has an optional `Tags:` line now.

Checks: 473 tests (new ones cover parseWhere ways in, openGoal, curated lookups, a validity check of `curated.json`, the tag rules, and the page's tag filter). Build and smoke pass, and smoke now clicks a tag on the story page.

changes.title: Say how to add something new on screen: grow Action, one case in runAction
changes.summary:
Closes a gap in the "what {A} does is data" rules. Nothing said what to do when a character needs something no `Action` can show yet, like a second mini game or a new kind of screen. An agent following the guard might have pushed it into `do` by reaching into React state, or decided it was blocked.

Now three places give the same answer: `src/game/CLAUDE.md` (a new section, "Something new on screen"), the comment at the top of `src/game/actions.ts`, and the guard's failure message. The answer:
1. Add the new value or kind to `Action`.
2. Add one case to App's `runAction`, plus its overlay. This is allowed, because the guard only blocks branches in `onInteract`.
3. Return it from the plugin's `act()`, test it with `pick()`, and optionally add a `?open=` link.

Docs and comments only, no behaviour change. 473 tests pass and the type check is clean.

Mike: heads-up. This is guidance your Claude will read when a character needs a new screen.

changes.title: One home each for random numbers, storage, the speech bubble and story dates; fewer kept chunks
changes.summary:
First PR from the code review. Nothing should look or play differently.

- **Chunk memory (phones):** the map keeps at most 16 drawn chunks instead of 40, so at most about 64 MB of canvas instead of about 160 MB. iPhone Safari drops canvases past roughly 256–384 MB in total. At most 4 chunks are ever on screen.
- **`src/city/random.ts`:** the six seeded random streams and hashes (`rng`, `lehmer`, `tileHash`, `intsHash`, `stringHash`, `nameHash`) now live in one module. They used to be spread across npcs, tileArt, chickenBoxing, visitors, ParkScene and the clock. Their formulas are unchanged, and `random.test.ts` pins their values from before the move, so houses, trees, fields and scarves stay the same.
- **`src/city/stored.ts`:** browser storage that never throws. It replaces eight hand-written try/catch copies in Cone Catch, the three arcade cabinets, the mute switch, your rabbit's look, the hint arrow and "hide other rabbits".
- **`drawSpeech()` in `tinyFont.ts`:** the pegasus's and the mermaids' identical speech bubble, now written once. I checked the mermaid's bubble in Chrome. Other rabbits' emote bubbles stack and lift, so they keep their own.
- **`src/story/dates.mjs`:** the story page and the recorder share `seattleDay`, `dateLabel`, `dayLabel`, `daysBetween` and `waitDays`. Before, each had its own copy.
- **Race result:** it now goes through `runAction(talk(…))` like every other dialog, instead of building the overlay by hand in App.tsx.
- **Docs:** the area notes say to use these helpers, so agents won't write new copies.

Mike: heads-up. The arcade cabinets and Cone Catch now save their best scores with `storedNumber` / `store`.

481 tests pass, and the build and smoke test pass. The preview comment script still works.

changes.title: Every three.js scene extends PixelScene: one renderer setup, loop, drag and dispose
changes.summary:
Third PR from the code review (item 5). The six three.js scenes (the Duck Arcade, Duck on the Moon, the cup, the park and both Luna rides) each repeated the same setup and teardown. That code now lives once in `src/experiences/pixelScene.ts`:
- **`PixelScene` base class:** sets up the renderer (1/3 size for the pixel look, or `smooth` for Duck on the Moon), fits it on resize, and runs the frame loop with a capped `dt` (`frame(dt, time)`; the base renders after). It also tracks drags (`this.drag({ onDrag, onEnd, capture })`), keeps listeners (`this.listen`), and frees everything on `dispose()`. Extra cleanup goes in `teardown()`: the orbit controls, the cup's paint texture, the arcade's ceiling video.
- **`disposeTree`:** frees every geometry, material and texture. The scenes' own cleanups had drifted apart: some only freed `map` textures, some skipped lines or sprites, and the cup and arcade left a canvas listener behind.
- **`Glance`:** the Luna rides' identical "drag to glance, then drift back", written once.

The arcade keeps its own details on top: no looking round while the bear offers, a click (not a drag) on the bag takes a licorice, and a hand cursor over the bag.

That's 9 files, +301 −398. `src/experiences/CLAUDE.md` now points new scenes at the base class.

Checks:
- New tests cover `Glance` (limits, drift back) and `disposeTree` (meshes with material arrays, lines, points, sprites, every texture). 486 tests pass.
- The build passes, and the smoke test passes (the arcade, every cabinet, the bear's licorice, a ride).
- In Chrome, each of the six scenes renders at the right size (320×200 for 960×600; Duck on the Moon at full size), dragging turns the view, leaving works, and no errors are logged. I compared screenshots of all six with before.

Mike: heads-up. A new 3D scene starts from `PixelScene`.

changes.title: Plugins change the map through one helper: walkway, solid, oncePerWorld
changes.summary:
Last item from the code review (item 8). Five plugins change map tiles when they start: the rowboat's dock, the forest maze, Luna Park, the garden and the boxing ring. Each wrote `world.tiles` by hand, with two copies of a once-per-map guard and edge checks in only one place. Luna Park also added its street name again on React's dev double start: `world.names` had "Luna Park" twice.

Now they all use `src/city/world/edit.ts` (tested):
- `walkway(world, name, cells)`: walkable ground under a street sign. The name is added once, so running it again reuses it.
- `solid(world, cells, { only })`: ground nobody walks through, optionally only over one kind of tile (the garden only clears park).
- `cellsIn(x, y, w, h)` and `oncePerWorld(world, key, make)`. The second replaces the rowboat's and the maze's own WeakMaps.
- All of them skip cells off the map.

`createIsland` now notes where plugin order matters: the garden comes before the squirrels, and the rowboat before the mermaids. `src/city/CLAUDE.md` tells new plugins to use the helper and never write `world.tiles` by hand.

**The map comes out identical.** I fingerprinted the finished map in a dev build on this branch and on `main`, and both have the same tile hash and the same street name on every tile (711748511). The only difference is 304 names instead of 305: no duplicate "Luna Park".

489 tests pass, and the build and smoke test pass.

changes.title: Story page: grab the before/after line and drag it
changes.summary:
On the story page, the line in a before/after photo is now what you drag. Before this, it only marked the spot and you moved it with the slider under the photo.

- Grab the knob on the line, or press anywhere on the photo, and drag left or right. The drag keeps going if your pointer leaves the photo.
- On a phone, a sideways swipe drags the line and an up-down swipe still scrolls the page.
- Keyboard: tab to the line, then the arrows move it 5% (Shift for 1%), and Home/End go to the ends. Screen readers see it as a slider.
- The slider under the photo is gone. Small "before" and "after" labels sit in the photo's bottom corners and fade when the line covers them.

Checked in Chrome on the live story log: mouse drag, a drag past the edge (stops at 100), a click (jumps to 20%), the arrow keys, End, and a touch swipe on a phone-sized screen (50 → 14). No page errors. The position math is pure and tested (`wipeAt`, `wipeKey` in `src/story/model.ts`).
